reconciliation: The frozen r01 patch is the corrected replacement for the stale run wording about emitting sequential indices: it directly emits the selected provider output_index, including explicit zero. That earlier defect is not present in e7881343. This review rejects r01 for a different defect: lifecycle state is still kind-wide rather than per provider output item, so same-kind interleaving violates the locked contract.
tests_reviewed: go test ./internal/translator/codex/claude -run 'Test.*(OutputIndex|Interleav|ContentBlock)' -count=1 on independently reconstructed result (pass)
go test ./internal/translator/codex/claude -count=1 on independently reconstructed result (pass)
independent adversarial same-kind lifecycle tests on the reconstructed result (fail as documented in findings)
nonstream conversion code has no patch hunk and existing package nonstream regressions pass

findings.claim: Text and function-call lifecycle indices are stored in one scalar slot per kind. Two active items of the same kind therefore collapse onto the first slot, and a missing done event leaves that slot stale so the next provider output_index does not win.
findings.proof: Independent reconstructed-result probes produced function-call indices [4,4,4,4,4,4,4,7] instead of [4,4,7,7,4,7,4,7], text indices [2,2,2,2,2,5] instead of [2,5,2,5,2,5], and a second function-call start at provider index 9 emitted [3,3] after an earlier index-3 item omitted done.
findings.required_fix: Track selected index and related lifecycle state per provider output item using stable item identity/output_index rather than one kind-wide slot. Explicit provider indices, including zero, must remain independent; use sequential fallback only for an item whose provider index is absent; reset only that item's state. Add two-function-call, two-text-item, explicit-zero-under-interleaving, missing-start, and missing-done regressions.

findings.claim: A later reasoning output_item.added directly overwrites the single active ThinkingBlockIndex and ThinkingSignature. Final signature_delta/content_block_stop events for the earlier reasoning item can therefore be emitted with the later item's index.
findings.proof: With reasoning item 4 open, adding reasoning item 6 changed the emitted sequence to [4,4,6,6,6]; the first item's final signature and stop should have retained index 4. This also shows reasoning finalization is not item-owned.
findings.required_fix: Make reasoning summary/signature/open/pending/finalization state item-scoped and finalize each reasoning lifecycle with its own selected index. Add same-kind reasoning interleaving and finalization tests, including absent summary-part start/done events.

findings.claim: The added interleaving test covers only one reasoning, one function call, and one text lifecycle. Its flattened index list cannot establish ownership when two items share a kind, so it misses both blocking defects and reset leakage.
findings.required_fix: Assert event type plus item/lifecycle identity and index for concurrent same-kind items; cover both completion orders, missing start/done events, explicit zero after another active item, reasoning finalization, and sequential fallback only when output_index is absent.

test_limitations: A broad go test ./... from the immutable tree cannot compile packages importing internal/managementasset because generated static/management.html is absent from the tree; this is unrelated to the two-file patch and is not treated as a patch finding.
